title: GigaWorld-1: World Models as Robot Policy Evaluators
hook: Testing a robot policy for real means slow, costly rollouts. GigaWorld-1 asks whether a video world model can judge a policy instead — and finds visual realism is the wrong thing to optimize for.
key_points: Systematic study of video world models as surrogate evaluators for robot policies, avoiding costly real-world rollouts.
Introduces WMBench, a benchmark built from real-robot teleoperation data and matched policy rollouts, for controlled comparisons.
Analyzes 7 world models and 4 action-representation schemes across 324,000+ simulated rollouts checked against real robot executions.
Key finding: evaluator quality tracks long-horizon, action-faithful rollout consistency — not short-term visual realism.
Pretraining gains come from balancing general world knowledge with robot-specific controllability, not data scale alone.
Releases GigaWorld-1, a world model optimized for policy evaluation, plus code, datasets, and toolkits.
content_html: Robot foundation models are hard to evaluate: unlike language models, which can be scored on digital benchmarks, robotic policies need slow, costly, hardware-limited real-world rollouts. That bottleneck has pushed interest toward using video world models as surrogate evaluators — but nobody had systematically checked what makes one trustworthy for the job.
extra_html: GigaWorld-1's team builds WMBench, a benchmark constructed from real-robot teleoperation data and matched policy rollouts, enabling controlled comparisons across model families, action encodings, rollout horizons, and evaluation metrics. Using it, they analyze 7 video world models, 4 action-representation schemes, and more than 324,000 simulated rollouts checked against real robot executions — further enriched with community submissions from the CVPR 2026 GigaBrain Challenge and over 12,000 hours of curated training video. Three findings stand out: evaluator quality is dominated by long-horizon, action-faithful rollout consistency rather than short-term visual realism; pretraining gains come from balancing general world knowledge against robot-specific controllability, not data scale alone; and architectural choices — action encoding, memory design, evaluator-focused post-training — strongly determine how well a world model aligns with real robot behavior. The team turns these findings into a design roadmap and realizes it in GigaWorld-1, a world model purpose-built for policy evaluation, releasing code, models, datasets, and toolkits. GigaWorld Team and colleagues, arXiv 2026 (31 HF community upvotes).

related.title: World Action Models: A Survey
related.hook: Robots are learning to imagine the future before acting. This survey untangles 'world action models' from video generators and VLA policies — and finds them converging on one idea.

related.title: RynnWorld-4D: RGB-Depth-Flow World Models for Robot Manipulation
related.hook: A robot needs to know how a scene's 3D structure will move, not just what it looks like. This world model predicts RGB, depth, and optical flow together, then hands the result straight to a policy.

related.title: RynnWorld-Teleop: Digital Teleoperation for Robot Data
related.hook: Collecting robot demonstrations means binding an operator's time to one physical robot. RynnWorld-Teleop swaps in a world model: move your hands, and it generates the footage instead.

flashcards.prompt: Why do the authors want a world model to serve as a robot policy evaluator?
flashcards.back_html: Evaluating robot policies normally requires slow, costly, hardware-limited real-world rollouts. A reliable world-model evaluator could substitute for many of them, making evaluation faster and cheaper.

flashcards.prompt: According to GigaWorld-1's WMBench analysis, what actually predicts whether a world model is a good policy evaluator?

choices.text: Long-horizon, action-faithful rollout consistency — not short-term visual realism
How many parameters the world model has
How fast the model renders each frame

flashcards.explanation_html: Across 7 world models and 324,000+ matched rollouts, the strongest predictor of evaluator reliability was staying action-faithful over long horizons, not producing visually realistic frames.

flashcards.prompt: Besides rollout consistency, what other factor did the study find shapes a good policy-evaluator world model?
flashcards.back_html: Pretraining gains depend not just on data scale but on balancing general world knowledge with robot-specific controllability — plus architectural choices like action encoding and memory design.
